claims.text: What the strip looks like A flat line — confirm it in more than one lead to exclude a disconnected lead.
claims.quote: Asystole: Flat line (conﬁrm in more than one lead to exclude lead disconnection).

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Prolonged VF loses amplitude and ultimately degenerates into asystole
claims.quote: Prolonged ventricular fibrillation results in decreasing waveform amplitude, from initial coarse VF to fine VF, ultimately degenerating into asystole

claims.text: Children: arrests are most often asphyxial — typically a bradyarrhythmia, then asystole
claims.quote: In children, who most often have asphyxial causes of cardiac arrest, the presenting rhythm is typically a bradyarrhythmia followed by asystole.

claims.text: Potentially treatable causes (“Hs and Ts”): hypoxia, hypovolemia, acidosis, hyperkalemia or hypokalemia, hypothermia; tablets/toxins, cardiac tamponade, tension pneumothorax, thrombosis (pulmonary or coronary)
claims.quote: The patient is evaluated for potentially treatable causes; a useful memory aid is "Hs and Ts": H:Hypoxia, hypovolemia, acidosis (hydrogen ion), hyperkalemia or hypokalemia, hypothermia T:Tablet or toxin ingestion, cardiac tamponade, tension pneumothorax, thrombosis (pulmonary or coronary)

claims.text: Symptoms Cardiac arrest: unconscious, apneic, pulseless; no measurable blood pressure; pupils dilated and unreactive
claims.quote: Diagnosis of cardiac arrest is by clinical findings of unconsciousness, apnea, and pulselessness. Arterial pressure is not measurable. Pupils dilate and become unreactive to light.

claims.text: Treatment CPR: rapid, uninterrupted chest compressions (“push hard and push fast”)
claims.quote: rapid initiation of uninterrupted chest compressions ("push hard and push fast")

claims.text: Non-shockable rhythms: give epinephrine early — linked to better neurologically intact survival
claims.quote: For non-shockable rhythms, early administration of epinephrine has been associated with improved neurologically intact survival

claims.text: Treat primary causes (e.g., hypoxia, hypovolemia, toxins, tamponade) promptly
claims.quote: primary causes (eg, hypoxia, hypovolemia, toxins, tamponade) must be promptly treated

claims.text: Prognosis: asystole after an unwitnessed out-of-hospital arrest — survival is unlikely
claims.quote: When factors are uniformly unfavorable (eg, patient in asystole after unwitnessed, out-of-hospital arrest), survival is unlikely.

notes.resolution: quote extended with the preceding line; claim reworded to "Potentially treatable causes"; re-checked pass
